clue.text: Tries for a strike — what can you expect?

definitions.meaning: a miner who searches for a gold strike is out prospecting
your outlook, the likely future in store

explanation.definitionFit: To prospect is to search for minerals, a strike being a find; one's prospects are future expectations.

clue.text: Assume I'll be in job

indicators.note: the clue says the letter will be in, so it is placed inside the word for a job

parts.note: a post is a job or position
the I of I'll, which (will) be in

explanation.surface: Someone takes it for granted they will land the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward as a premise, i.e. to suppose something is so.

clue.text: Annoying effect of seat being taken by neutral party

parts.words: seat being taken by neutral party
parts.note: someone neutral is said to sit on the fence, so the fence is their seat

explanation.surface: Someone is irritated when their seat is grabbed by a person who will not take sides.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'sitting on the fence' (refusing to take sides) makes the fence the neutral party's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving offence is causing annoyance or resentment, the result of a slight.

clue.text: Actor, say — place for me in right theatre coming up?.

indicators.note: the clue tells us to place the words for me in between the other pieces
in a down clue coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor wonders whether a job is coming up for them at a decent theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns REP into PER; 'place ... in' puts FOR ME between PER and R.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is one example of a performer, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Supporter of something wicked

parts.note: read 'wicked' as having a wick: the holder that props up a wax light

explanation.definitionFit: A candlestick holds up a candle, which is the thing with a wick.

clue.text: Dry period, very short

definitions.meaning: of wine, not sweet, from the French word
a moment, abbreviated from the time unit of sixty to the minute

explanation.surface: A drought that does not last long.
explanation.definitionFit: Sec describes dry wine, and is also a clipped form of 'second', a brief moment.

clue.text: Admiralty secretary has furtive look, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: someone who sneaks a glance peeps

explanation.surface: A naval official is caught sneaking a glance at something.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Pepys, the 17th-century diarist, was Secretary to the Admiralty; his name is pronounced 'peeps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepys held the post of Secretary of the Admiralty under Charles II and James II.

clue.text: King embraced by parents in Italian city

indicators.note: one piece is hugged by the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: pa and ma, the two parents
R is the abbreviation for king (Rex)

explanation.surface: A monarch is hugged by his mother and father in an Italian town.
explanation.definitionFit: Parma is a city in Emilia-Romagna, famous for ham and cheese.

clue.text: Caesar's force in unusually poor condition

indicators.note: the Latin word sits in the middle of the rearranged letters
signals the letters of the next word are arranged in an unusual way

parts.note: vis is Latin for force, the language Caesar spoke

explanation.surface: A Roman army is in unusually bad shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges POOR into PRO-O, and VIS goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a stipulation or condition attached to an agreement.

clue.text: Inasmuch as reply is heartless, wrong way to sign off?

parts.note: since means inasmuch as, because

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter of the word goes

parts.note: taken as written before its centre is removed

explanation.surface: If your reply lacks feeling, ending it warmly would be the wrong touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes P, the central letter of REPLY, leaving RELY. The question mark: ending a cold letter 'Yours sincerely' would be the wrong sign-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter's closing formula is often 'Yours sincerely', ironic below an unfeeling letter.

clue.text: Bearing endless insult can make one colour

parts.note: S, south, is a compass bearing

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter

parts.note: an affront is an insult

explanation.surface: Putting up with constant abuse can turn someone a different shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron is an orange-yellow shade named after the spice.

clue.text: Film shows Dickensian hero without love

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: Sydney Carton, hero of A Tale of Two Cities
O, the zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A movie depicts a lonely Dickens protagonist with no romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: CARTON goes around O.
explanation.definitionFit: An animated movie is called a cartoon.

clue.text: Take steps to make colour disappear

parts.note: tan is a light brown shade
to go is to vanish

explanation.surface: Measures are being taken to remove a stain or dye.
explanation.definitionFit: To tango is to dance it, so to take dance steps.

clue.text: Though a pound short, victualler may be making profit

indicators.note: suggests the letters may be rearranged into another word
one letter of the word goes missing

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound (libra)

explanation.surface: A publican is doing well despite being a pound down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' removes one L from VICTUALLER; 'may be' rearranges the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucrative business is a money-making one.

clue.text: Car not fixed …

definitions.meaning: a motor with a folding roof
able to be changed into another form

explanation.surface: A vehicle that has not been repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: A convertible is a soft-top car, and anything convertible can be changed rather than being permanent.

clue.text: Fear of a pair at bridge

parts.note: West and East form one of the two partnerships in the card game

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about a couple of card players.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the four seats are North, South, East and West; W and E play as partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Awe is reverential dread or wonder.

clue.text: entailed a modification, so driven away

indicators.note: a modification changes the order of the letters given

explanation.surface: A change was needed, so people were pushed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Alienated people have been estranged, made to feel they do not belong.

clue.text: Mixed metaphors in Moliere's work

indicators.note: mixed up, so the letters that follow are jumbled

explanation.surface: A critic finds muddled imagery in a French playwright's writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Misanthrope is a 1666 comedy by Molière.

clue.text: He had to change editor, being rash

indicators.note: the letters given are changed around

explanation.surface: Someone impulsively replaced their editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot-headed people act impetuously, without thinking.

clue.text: Off point in Solent, in a word

definitions.meaning: the two words run together make a word meaning cheeky or rude

explanation.definitionFit: Impertinent means irrelevant (not pertinent) and also rude, as is someone insolent.

clue.text: Going to uncle for quiet and shelter

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
an awning is a canvas shelter

explanation.surface: Visiting a relative to get some peace and a roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker, so going to uncle is pawning one's goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Pawning goods means taking them to a pawnbroker, jokingly called 'uncle'.

clue.text: Middle girl of three seen together on calendar

definitions.text: Middle girl of three seen together on calendar

parts.words: Middle girl of three seen together on calendar
parts.note: three consecutive months are also girls' names; the middle one is wanted

explanation.definitionFit: April, May and June are both girls' names and consecutive months, and the middle one is May.

clue.text: Put me on ship in a Mediterranean port

parts.note: SS, steamship

explanation.surface: Book me a passage to a southern European harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Messina is a port city in Sicily on the strait of the same name.

clue.text: Additional demand for one course …

parts.note: new can mean additional, as in a new supply
a market for goods is the demand for them

explanation.surface: Extra appetite for a single dish at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket in Suffolk is the home of British horse racing; 'course' means racecourse, not part of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket is a famous racecourse, one of many in Britain.

clue.text: Wrongly equated with a mile?

definitions.meaning: from the proverb that a narrow failure is as good as a mile

explanation.surface: Someone mistakenly measures something as a mile.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'a miss is as good as a mile' says a near miss is still a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiss means wrongly, and 'a miss' is what the proverb equates with a mile.

clue.text: … or another — record so many

parts.note: EP, an extended-play record
taken as written
M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a great number set another record.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues 20 across: one course (NEWMARKET) ... or another, i.e. a second racecourse; Epsom in Surrey hosts the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs is another English racecourse, home of the Derby.

clue.text: Power of 19 ac in past

definitions.meaning: the past tense of the modal verb from 19 across

explanation.surface: Strength drawn from the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Might is strength, and it is also the past form of the modal verb may.

clue.text: College crowd?

definitions.meaning: a college at Cambridge, Oxford or Dublin
from the saying that two is company, three a crowd

explanation.surface: A gathering of students.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinity is a college name at several universities, and a trinity is a group of three, which the saying calls a crowd.

clue.text: Agreeable reply? No, it is not

definitions.text: Agreeable reply? No, it is not

parts.words: Agreeable reply? No, it is not
parts.note: a word of assent, which is the opposite of saying no

explanation.definitionFit: Yes is the reply that agrees, and it is precisely not 'no'.

clue.text: Command no passes

definitions.meaning: in bridge, the auction when players make calls instead of passing

explanation.surface: An order that nobody may get by.
explanation.definitionFit: Bidding is an order (do my bidding), and in card games bidding is making offers rather than passing.

clue.text: Artist from abroad eg a sculptor

indicators.note: the letters come from within the following words

explanation.surface: A foreign sculptor, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgar Degas, the French painter of dancers, also made sculptures.
explanation.definitionFit: Degas was a French Impressionist painter and sculptor.

clue.text: Firm dates arranged quickly

indicators.note: the letters given are arranged afresh

parts.note: fast means quickly

explanation.surface: A company that sets up appointments at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadfast means firm and unwavering.
